title: District-level Climate Risk Assessment for India: Mapping Flood and Drought Risks released
organization: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India
temporal_coverage: District risk analysis uses flood and drought hazard records from 1970–2019; summary released December 2024.
methodology: Government release summarizing a district assessment by IIT Mandi, IIT Guwahati and CSTEP.
limitations: Risk bands are comparative; the release summarizes rather than reproduces the underlying report.

title: How Extreme Heat is Impacting India: Assessing District-level Heat Risk
organization: Council on Energy, Environment and Water (CEEW)
temporal_coverage: District heat trends for 1982–2022; socio-economic and health indicators include Census 2011 and NFHS 2019–21.
methodology: CEEW district heat-risk index using 35 hazard, exposure and vulnerability indicators.
limitations: Relative bands, dated indicators; state findings need validation.

title: Mitigating the Urban Heat Island Effect in Indian Cities
organization: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India
temporal_coverage: HAP status reported July 2026; Delhi climate vulnerability assessment uses 1991–2020 observations and projections to mid-century.
methodology: Ministry press release summarizing heat-action-plan status and the Delhi SAPCC 2.0 assessment.
limitations: Ministry-reported plan counts and planned measures do not establish effectiveness or completed outcomes.

title: NHRC calls for preventive measures by 11 States to protect vulnerable people from heat waves
organization: National Human Rights Commission of India
temporal_coverage: Heat risks and NCRB death data for 2018–2022; NHRC intervention issued May 2025.
methodology: NHRC press release describing its communication to state governments and cited NCRB figures.
limitations: The reported death count is attributed to NCRB; NHRC's requested measures are not evidence of implementation.

title: Climate and Gender: Association Between Droughts and Intimate Partner Violence in India
organization: American Journal of Epidemiology / National Library of Medicine PubMed Central
temporal_coverage: National Family Health Survey rounds 2015–2016 and 2019–2021; article published November 2023.
methodology: Cross-sectional analysis of 122,696 married women, combining survey IPV reports with precipitation-based and government socioeconomic drought classifications.
limitations: Self-reported and cross-sectional data limit generalizability and causal inference; household income pathway was not tested.
